tier5.interpretation: Identical accuracy across 3 reasoning formats proves the classifier uses a deterministic 3-rule heuristic, not reasoning. The 46.4% is inside a 44-51% bias-swing range driven entirely by default-guess choice.

tier6.interpretation: Random Forest achieves 42.9% with symmetric ciphers at random-guess floor (15-25%). No hidden statistical signal exists. Feature importance confirms file_size is dominant. LLM's 46.4% exceeds honest ceiling due to confabulation bias.

scaling.hypothesis: The information-theoretic ceiling will hold or strengthen at scale. A larger corpus should not reveal emergent signals, because modern ciphers are designed to be statistically indistinguishable regardless of sample size.

variant_testing.finding: RANDOM GUESSING (52.9%) OUTPERFORMS CLAUDE'S DETERMINISTIC HEURISTIC (48.6%)
variant_testing.interpretation: The deterministic heuristic (always AES-128 for mod16==0) nails one class and misses four others. Random guessing, by giving each class a fair chance, achieves higher overall accuracy. Forced reasoning costs 7.1 pp relative to honest ignorance.

final_verdict.honest_ceiling: 55.7% (human expert: deterministic on unique sizes + random on overlaps)
final_verdict.llm_heuristic_ceiling: 48.6% (actively harmful due to negative inductive bias)
final_verdict.conclusion: No reasoning style, no feature engineering, and no model choice can extract signal that does not exist. The best strategy on symmetric ciphers is either random guessing or honest admission of ignorance.
